question.text: A radioactive element <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi><mprescripts></mprescripts><mn>92</mn><mn>242</mn></mmultiscripts></math> emits two <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math>-particles, one electron and two positrons. The product nucleus is represented by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">Y</mi><mprescripts></mprescripts><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mn>234</mn></mmultiscripts></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> is ______.

solution.text:
When a radioactive nucleus emits 1 α-particle, its mass number decreases by 4 and the atomic number decreases by 2. During positron emission, the mass number remains unchanged but the atomic number decreases by 1. Similarly, during electron emission, the mass number remains unchanged but the atomic number decreases by 1.

So, the value of P=92-2-2+1-1-1

⇒P=92-5

⇒P=87.
